value.title: PR 133 repair still needs recipient-pinned notice recovery

sections.name: body
sections.value:
PR 133 repair review remains blocked at 44f1eea35be87355a9871c4fc7fdb1616fc9749f. F001 is closed by atomic unanswered admission. F002 ordinary missing-target/failure retry and interrupted pre-admission claims are repaired, but accepted-notice replay across PA rotation remains unsafe.

An admitted notice to PA A can lose its final stamp during daemon interruption. The only persisted notification claim is a timestamp, not its recipient. After lease expiry and PA rotation to B, notice resolves B and sends role-limit-notice-ID again. Delivery deduplicates by recipient and id, so both PA inboxes admit it. Persist/reconcile the notification recipient across admission and retry, using existing recipient-scoped admission evidence, and add an admitted-but-unstamped notice plus rotation CI case. This finding is source/dataflow proof, not a local reproduction.

The gone-holder path is acceptable: it waits until due, reports the actual absence without a fabricated check-in, leaves checkin_at unset, stops nothing and retries if nobody can be told.

Exact-head CI run 42201776537 and JUnit artifact 13494408121 confirm all four new HTTP regressions and the new store claim case pass. 1986 tests pass overall, five skipped globally, four jobs green. Those tests cover no-recipient and pre-admission recovery, not admitted-notice recipient rotation. Live-holder check-in admission failure remains an acknowledged proof gap. No local builds/tests/probes were run. Output: roles/reviewer/outputs/2026-11/pr-133-44f1eea-delta.md.
